subject: Prod: p99 spike during evening - circuit-breaker hits
messages:
From: ops@ldaptive.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.choi@ldaptive.com
Date: 2027-05-29T21:18:00-04:00
Subject: Prod alert - evening p99 spike and intermittent 502s

Hi Jasmine / Lauren,

We started seeing a sustained p99 increase (~1.8s -> ~4.5s) across our production endpoints between 19:45-20:30 ET tonight. Additionally, ~1% of requests returned 502s for ~10 minutes. We capture a few traces attached (perf-dump-0529.tar.gz) and a short summary below.

Observed:
- Traffic: steady, no big surge in RPS (within expected 5% window)
- Errors: 502s concentrated on the /generate route
- Latency: p50 ~200ms, p95 ~820ms, p99 ~4.5s (baseline ~1.2s)

Impact: customer-facing timeouts and increased retries. This is the highest severity for us tonight. Could you confirm this is on Redwood side and share any immediate mitigations?

Thanks,
Aaron Park
Ldaptive Ops
attachments: perf-dump-0529.tar.gz (log bundle), p99-traces.json
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: ops@ldaptive.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-29T21:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Prod alert - evening p99 spike and intermittent 502s

Aaron — thanks for the signal and the traces. We're looking immediately. Initial acknowledgement and plan:

1) I'm opening an internal investigation with infra/serving (cc'd).
2) Can you confirm whether you were using any new routing rules or large-batch jobs tonight? Any sudden change in prompt length distribution?
3) As a quick mitigation, are you OK if we temporarily increase the concurrency cap for your account by 2x and enable the fallback route to the dedicated vpool for 30 mins? This avoids client-side retries and should lower queueing pressure.

I'll share an update within 30 minutes.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-29T22:10:00-04:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage - queueing/backpressure signal

Quick notes from the infra runbook after ingesting the dump:
- We see sustained head-of-line queue growth on the pod group serving ldaptive (avg queue depth jumped from 2 -> 18 during window).
- Connection logs show a consistent pattern: batch window extended due to a handful of high-token requests -> KV cache pressure -> some requests stalled waiting for GPU kernel and then tripped the circuit-breaker (502).
- Concurrency cap for the account is 24; at peak we hit 24 consistently and the autoscaler didn't spin up new workers due to transient GPU allocation latency.
- No sign the model itself crashed; more of a serving throughput bottleneck combined with backpressure propagation across shared pools.

Attachments: p99-traces.json (sample traces pointing to long compile/queue waits).

Recommended immediate actions (short-lived, <1hr):
- Increase account concurrency cap to 48 (temporary) to reduce queue head accumulation.
- Activate dedicated pool fallback (route 10% -> dedicated vpool, then ramp if stable).
- Kick a targeted autoscale policy refresh for the pod group (force new nodes).

I'll start the autoscale refresh now and prepare a mitigation playbook.

— Rishi Malhotra
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: ops@ldaptive.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T00:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Prod alert - evening p99 spike and intermittent 502s

Aaron — quick update and proposed mitigation:

What we found: queueing + concurrency cap hit -> circuit-breaker -> 502s. Rishi confirms no model regression.

Immediate fixes we want to apply (need your OK):
- Temporary concurrency cap increase from 24 -> 48 for the next 60 minutes.
- Route 25% of your traffic to your dedicated vpool (isolates you from shared pool backpressure) and monitor.
- Force an autoscale refresh on the serving cluster (should add capacity within 8–12 minutes).

If you approve we'll apply now and monitor closely; we'll also send a post-incident summary and discuss whether a Reserved/Dedicated plan or a revised autoscale policy would prevent recurrence.

Playbook reference: playbook_circuit-breaker.md (link attached).

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ops@ldaptive.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.choi@ldaptive.com, accounts@ldaptive.com
Date: 2027-05-30T00:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Prod alert - evening p99 spike and intermittent 502s

Jasmine — thanks. Please proceed with the temporary cap increase and routing to the dedicated vpool. We approve the changes for 60 minutes. We'll expect a short post-incident report and would like to discuss credits for customer-impact minutes during the window.

— Aaron Park
Ldaptive Ops
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Prod alert - exec summary & ask for SLA exception / reserved capacity discussion

Team — forwarding the thread and summarizing for exec attention:

Summary: Tonight between ~19:45–20:30 ET Ldaptive saw p99 jumps to ~4.5s and ~1% 502s due to queueing/backpressure after a handful of high-token requests caused extended batch windows. Account hit the concurrency cap (24) and the autoscaler lagged during transient GPU allocation. Rishi applied mitigations (temp cap -> 48, route 25% to dedicated vpool, forced autoscale refresh). Immediate recovery: p99 returned to baseline within ~10 minutes after routing.

Impact: customer-visible slowdowns and retries; business is asking for credits for impacted minutes and wants a plan to avoid recurrence. They are an active expansion candidate (deal D-78321).

Asks for leadership:
1) Approve a follow-up discussion with Sales + Finance to consider a one-off credit for the impacted window (we should estimate token/time impact).
2) Approve a short-term Dedicated capacity trial or revised autoscale guardrails for this account (they're pushing for predictability).
3) Support from Product/Infra to prioritize a mitigation: reduce autoscaler cold-start latency and add a soft-shed policy to prevent cascading circuit-breaker trips.

I'll draft a customer-facing post-incident summary and a recommended commercial offer (trial + reduced price for first month) if you approve the above.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
